question.problem: Use the difference of squares method to solve the equation $16{y}^{2}-81=0.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the difference of squares formula, we factor the left-hand side of our quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}16{y}^{2}-81 & =0 \\ (4y)^{2}-(9)^{2} & =0 \\ (4y-9)(4y+9) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the zero product rule, we have

$$
4y-9=0\,\text{or}\,4y+9=0.
$$

Then, we solve each equation separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}4y-9 & =0 & \, & \, & 4y+9 & =0 \\ 4y & =9 & \, & \, & 4y & =-9 \\ y & =\frac{9}{4} & \, & \, & y & =-\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $y=-\frac{9}{4},\frac{9}{4}.$ We can write this even more concisely as $y=\pm \frac{9}{4}.$
